QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_17

question.text: Under SAS-400, the Sakhi case provides mental-health support to new mothers. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate OUTCOME indicator for this programme?

answer.text: Number of counselling sessions delivered (this is an output, not an outcome)
Number of counsellors trained (this is an input)
Improved mental health and coping mechanisms among new mothers, evidenced through pre- and post-engagement assessments of a defined sub-sample

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the workbook's input-output-outcome-impact chain, outcomes are changes in the condition of beneficiaries, not activity counts. In the SAS-400 Sakhi case, improved mental health and coping mechanisms among women, particularly new mothers, is the outcome that the assessor should evidence through baseline and end-line assessment of a defined sub-sample. The Trap: Option A counts sessions (an output), Option B counts trained counsellors (an input), and Option D is a cost ratio, not an outcome. Note: Pre-define how the change in mental health will be measured (a structured assessment at baseline and end-line on a defined sub-sample) so that the outcome can be evidenced consistently in the report.
